title: 资本观察：牛股风险提示不是“走过场”
content:
登录新浪财经APP 搜索【信披】查看更多考评等级
来源：资本秘闻
近日， 新华文轩 等多只牛股披露公告提示风险。但部分投资者对此不以为然，风险提示过后，市场对牛股的投机热情依旧不减。牛股的风险提示从来都不是“走过场”，它既是上市公司履行信披义务的硬性要求，也是为过度投机情绪降温的一种理性提示。
在部分短线投资者眼中，风险提示公告只是“例行公事”地走个过场，甚至有投资者把它当作“妖股通行证”。不仅仅是忽视风险提示，一种畸形的投机文化正在形成。上市公司越提示风险，资金炒作情绪反而越强烈，风险提示似乎成了股价继续上涨的发令枪，这是典型的无厘头炒作。
然而，从资本市场制度设计来看，风险提示是信息披露体系的重要一环，有着极强的严肃性和必要性，绝非形式化地“走过场”。
风险提示其实是上市公司的一道“必答题”。
A股监管规则明确要求，当个股短期出现大幅异常波动、市场炒作情绪过热、股价明显偏离合理估值区间时，上市公司必须及时自查经营情况、核实重大事项，并如实向市场披露潜在的风险。如果公司选择沉默，反而可能被监管问询，甚至可能构成信息披露违法违规。
上市公司披露的每一份风险提示公告，都需要经过内部严格的核查，内容真实客观，如实反映公司经营现状，澄清市场不实炒作，是维护市场信息透明、保护中小投资者的重要制度安排。
多数短期牛股的公司基本面未发生重大变化，股价却严重偏离正常估值，其始作俑者，是投机资金合力上演的击鼓传花。
面对高估的估值、非理性的炒作，上市公司进行风险提示，也是在为过度的投机炒作情绪降温。
相较于专业的机构投资者，中小投资者信息渠道有限、市场研判能力较弱，更容易被火热的题材概念误导，盲目跟风追高。上市公司风险提示的重要意义在于补齐中小投资者的信息短板，打破市场信息不对称的局面。
在市场炒作的狂热阶段，上市公司用权威的公告提示潜在风险，提醒投资者理性交易，遏制盲目投机行为。可以说，风险提示最大的保护对象，是缺乏风控能力的普通中小投资者。
当然，风险提示并不能完全阻止投机。市场里从来不缺追逐热点的投资者，他们或许会把风险提示当做“耳旁风”。但风险提示的意义，在于它为那些愿意冷静思考的投资者提供了必要的信息，为那些犹豫不决的投资者敲响了警钟。
更重要的是，当下A股监管生态持续升级。在上市公司风险提示的同时，还可能同步触发交易所的动态监控、重点核查以及专项监管和问询。
如此而来，上市公司以公告形式提示风险，叠加监管层动态监管，就形成了一种协同的风险防控体系，能够对非理性炒作形成有效震慑。这也意味着，风险提示是引导市场理性运行的重要信号，绝非投资者眼中的“走过场”。
面对牛股的风险提示，投资者不妨多一分敬畏。如果把牛股的风险提示当作“走过场”，吃亏的可能是投资者自己的“钱袋子”。

title: Andy Burnham signals he will fight election on tax rises to fund social care reform
content:
Jim Pickard and Chris Smyth in Liverpool

Published September 27 2026

Updated September 27 2026

Andy Burnham has admitted his plan to overhaul social care will not be delivered until after the next general election in a major delay to the prime minister’s signature policy pledge.

Burnham on Sunday signalled that Labour will fight the next election on a clear proposal to raise taxes specifically for a new social care system free at the point of use.

He said the shake-up of Britain’s beleaguered care system would be “hard” to do in this parliament and said he wanted to make it a Labour manifesto pledge at the next general election.

But delaying firm action beyond 2029 will prompt criticism given that Burnham seized the leadership of the Labour Party in July with a promise to move quickly and use “whatever political capital I have” to fix the crumbling care system.

“I have to keep people’s trust as well and there are commitments in the manifesto that would make it hard to do in this parliament,” he told the BBC’s Laura Kuenssberg on Sunday.

“So I’m saying to you that I will develop a very clear plan, and I will put that plan to the public at a general election. That will be where the plan gets tested and people will then be able to decide.”

On Friday, Burnham said the next general election would be in 2029 as he insisted that he would not go to the country in a snap contest.

The prime minister told the BBC that some voters would not support his plans for introducing a system of social care that will be free at the point of use, which is likely to cost billions of pounds. Burnham insisted it would cost less than the £18bn estimated by the Health Foundation think-tank.

“That is the way to do it . . . to get that endorsement and then introduce the system in the next parliament, because the backing of people for this really matters,” he said.

Burnham has already brought forward to next year a social care review by Whitehall troubleshooter Baroness Louise Casey.

Social care reform in England has led to political pain for various administrations over the last few decades.

As health secretary in 2010, Burnham proposed paying for a national care service through a levy on estates, which was branded a “death tax” by the Conservatives.

In 2017, then Conservative prime minister Theresa May’s attempt to push through a manifesto proposal to take the value of people’s houses into account in assessing eligibility for home care was dubbed a “dementia tax” and swiftly reversed.

Then after Boris Johnson made a pledge that people would not have to sell their homes to pay for care, he was forced by his chancellor, Rishi Sunak, to break a manifesto commitment by raising national insurance to pay for it to the dismay of his own party.

After years of failed attempts to reform social care, Caroline Abrahams of Age UK said Burnham’s commitments on the issue “suggest we are closer to the fundamental social care reform we need to see than we’ve been for a generation”.

However, shadow home secretary Chris Philp said tax increases would be a “red line” for the Conservatives and they would not “under any circumstances” support further rises.

He said the country is “already taxed too highly”, telling the BBC: “If more money is needed, for example, for social care or indeed for defence, we would find that money through savings elsewhere, particularly in the welfare budget.”

Reform UK’s shadow chancellor Robert Jenrick also criticised the prime minister, saying his plans for reforming social care amounted to a “universal death tax”.

“He’s too weak to cut the sky-high benefits bill,” Jenrick added.

“Instead of piling more taxes on hard-working families, we should be tackling wasteful spending and getting people off welfare and into work.”

Additional reporting by David Sheppard

title: VNA概念热度第一！东方中科等热门股紧急澄清
content:
记者丨林健民
编辑丨李燕娜
9月27日晚间，VNA（矢量网络分析仪）概念话题登顶 同花顺 热度榜单，2连板牛股 东方中科 （002819.SZ）亦发布异动公告称，其销售的VNA产品均为代理产品，公司不进行相关产品的生产制造。
公告显示，东方中科销售的矢量网络分析仪涉及国内外多个品牌，相关产品均为代理产品，非公司自研产品，公司不进行相关产品的生产制造。东方中科指出，相关矢量网络分析仪及其配件、软件及解决方案2025年销售收入为1.24亿元，占公司2025年营业收入的3.84%；2026年1—6月销售收入为4843.24万元，占公司2026年1—6月营业收入的3.62%。上述收入占比均较小，对公司业绩影响有限。
华泰证券 指出，VNA（矢量网络分析仪）是用于测量射频与微波器件电气网络参数的核心仪器，通过比较入射波、反射波与传输波的幅度及相位，判断被测器件的反射与传输特性，主要测试指标包括驻波比、S参数、阻抗、回波损耗、插入损耗及群时延等。随着数据中心网络向800G、1.6T演进，高速连接器、线缆及高端PCB对信号完整性与良率管控的要求持续提高，带动VNA测试需求增长。
市场方面，根据Future Market Insights预测，全球VNA市场2025年约9.01亿美元，2035年预计达到12.75亿美元，期间CAGR达3.5%，此前高端市场中是德科技、罗德与施瓦茨等海外龙头凭借较强的硬件技术及客户绑定占据市场较大份额。华泰证券判断，随着技术持续突破，国内企业市场份额有望提升，产业链相关公司包括 鼎阳科技 、 电科思仪 、 普源精电 等。
随着市场对VNA关注度的提高，部分概念股公司股价接连上涨。除东方中科外， 优利德 、电科思仪、鼎阳科技近日均因公司股票连续3个交易日内收盘价格涨幅偏离值累计达到30%而发布异动公告，并就VNA相关业务进行了回复。
优利德发布异动公告称，公司2026年上半年设立了天津研发中心，与成都研发中心协同开展射频测试仪器的技术研发，67GHz矢量网络分析仪目前处于研发阶段。研发进展、产品落地及市场推广均存在较大不确定性，项目短期内不会对公司业绩产生重大影响。公司已推出并销售矢量网络分析仪（VNA）产品，目前产品线主要包括VNA4000系列和VNA3000系列，主要面向无线通信、广播电视、汽车电子、半导体、医疗器件等领域射频器件及组件的研发与生产测试，提供性能测试方案。
电科思仪表示，公司研发生产的太赫兹矢量网络分析仪、信号发生器、频谱分析仪等系列化测试仪器，成果已应用于半导体测试、航空航天、通信等领域。
鼎阳科技表示，公司主营业务为数字示波器、矢量网络分析仪、波形和信号发生器、频谱分析仪、源表/可编程直流电源/源载模拟器、数字万用表、模块化仪器和电子负载等通用电子测试测量仪器的研发、生产和销售。公司是全球极少数具有数字示波器、信号发生器、频谱分析仪和矢量网络分析仪四大通用电子测试测量仪器主力产品研发、生产和销售能力的通用电子测试测量仪器厂家。

title: Swiss voters reject proposal to strengthen neutrality
content:
Mercedes Ruehl , Switzerland and Austria correspondent

Published September 27 2026

Updated September 27 2026

Swiss voters have rejected a proposal to impose strict new limits on the country’s centuries-old neutrality, deciding in a referendum to maintain their existing approach to sanctions and security co-operation with other European countries.

The initiative, conceived by Christoph Blocher, a rightwing billionaire and former government minister, would have enshrined “perpetual and armed” neutrality in the constitution and restricted the government’s freedom to decide what neutrality means in practice.

Blocher and Pro Schweiz, a sovereigntist group opposed to closer ties with the EU, collected enough signatures to force a national referendum. But the rightwing populist Swiss People’s Party (SVP), which opposed joining the EU’s sanctions on Russia, was the only big political party to support the proposal.

The initiative was decisively rejected, with 68.4 per cent of voters casting ballots against it as of Sunday afternoon, with 31.6 per cent in favour. It failed to win a majority in any of Switzerland’s 26 cantons. Turnout was 46.5 per cent.

Switzerland would have been barred from co-operating with military alliances unless it faced an attack or one was being prepared, and would be prevented from imposing sanctions unless they were approved by the UN.

The result leaves Switzerland with room to adapt its neutrality policy as Europe confronts a more uncertain security environment.

But the campaign revived a much older argument over what Swiss neutrality actually means — and the considerable flexibility with which the country has historically applied it.

Neutrality developed over centuries as a pragmatic means of protecting a small confederation divided by language and religion from the wars of its larger neighbours. It also helped insulate those internal divisions from conflicts beyond Switzerland’s borders.

The policy ensured Switzerland remained neutral during world wars. But its conduct — particularly during the second world war — undermined the idea that Swiss neutrality was ever absolute.

Successive governments have instead interpreted the policy according to circumstance. Switzerland remains outside Nato and the EU, but has joined Nato’s Partnership for Peace, participated in international peacekeeping and imposed sanctions on other countries.

That room for manoeuvre was at the heart of Sunday’s vote. The government argued that imposing a stricter constitutional definition would remove the flexibility that has allowed Switzerland to adapt to circumstances.

The tensions came to a head after Russia’s invasion in 2022. Switzerland’s decision to largely adopt EU sanctions against Moscow was controversial domestically and prompted Blocher’s campaign. Critics argued that Bern had compromised its neutrality.

For many in Switzerland’s internationally exposed business community, however, following western sanctions was pragmatic given the country’s dependence on European markets and a global financial system dominated by the US dollar.

The argument has become more consequential as European security has deteriorated. Bern has sought closer co-operation with its neighbours on air defence, cyber security and military interoperability — precisely the sort of flexibility that could have been constrained by the initiative.

Markus Mäder, Switzerland’s state secretary for security policy, told the FT this year that the country regarded itself as “an integral part of European security”.

The Swiss population has “firmly rejected isolation and remains committed to European co-operation”, said Beat Wittmann, chair of Swiss corporate advisory group Porta Advisors.

title: Ten climbers missing after avalanche hits Himalayan base camp
content:
At least 10 Nepali climbers who were preparing to lead an expedition are missing after an avalanche hit a base camp in the Himalayas on Sunday.

The climb's organisers said the local guides were at a staging point close to the Himlung Himal peak in Manang district when the avalanche struck on Sunday morning.

Forecasts showed there was heavy snowfall around the 7,126 metre (23,380ft) peak in recent days, which lies on Nepal's border with Tibet.

Poor weather has hampered rescue efforts, with helicopters and rescue teams unable to reach the site.

Bibhuti Chand Thakur, of Himalaya Holidays Trekking, told AFP news agency: "Eight members of our expedition team and two more from another company have been reported missing."

The Nepali team had been sent ahead of foreign climbers to prepare the camp, manage the route and fix ropes on the mountain.

Nepal's mountain districts have seen persistent rain and snow in recent days, creating treacherous conditions for the country's economically important climbing tourism industry.

Climbers were forced to leave Mount Manaslu, the eighth highest peak in the world, earlier this week due to the rising threat of avalanches.

The latest death of Nepali climbers comes less than two months after six lost their lives on Broad Peak in Pakistan, including renowned British-Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja.

Extreme weather further south in the neighbouring Indian region of Uttar Pradesh has killed more than 50 people, officials there said.

It comes as efforts to recover bodies continues on the Nepal-Tibet border, where more than 6,000 people are still missing after a massive flood and landslide in August.

More than 1,400 people are confirmed to have died after a glacial collapse in the Himalayas sent vast quantities of water and debris careering down the Trishuli River valley, sweeping away settlements.

title: 溢价744.44%！3.82亿重组上会迎考！
content:
来源：资本秘闻
筹划近两年时间， *ST禾信 发行股份购买资产事项迎来了上会机会，将于9月29日接受大考。据悉，公司拟收购上海量羲技术有限公司（以下简称“量羲技术”）56%的股权并募集配套资金，此次并购事项最终能否获得并购重组委放行，答案也即将揭晓。筹划重组背后，*ST禾信近年来业绩表现并不乐观，2022年以来，公司净利连亏四年，目前已被实施退市风险警示，上述重组也被市场认为是*ST禾信为保壳而采取的重要措施。
019月29日重组上会
根据安排，上交所并购重组委定于9月29日召开2026年第18次并购重组委审议会议，审议*ST禾信发行股份购买资产事项。
据*ST禾信最新披露的重组报告书（上会稿），公司拟通过发行股份及支付现金向吴明、上海堰岛共2名交易对方购买量羲技术56%的股权，并募集配套资金，交易价格约为3.82亿元。本次交易构成重大资产重组，预计构成关联交易。
回溯*ST禾信历史公告，公司自2024年10月便开始筹划上述重组事项，至今已历时近两年时间。
资料显示，量羲技术专注于极低温极微弱信号测量调控设备的研发、生产与销售。*ST禾信是一家集质谱仪研发、生产、销售及技术服务为一体的国家火炬计划重点高新技术企业。
*ST禾信表示，本次交易后，公司与标的公司通过优势技术协同提升上市公司产品性能、布局标的公司新技术路线，并整合客户及供应商资源，扩大整体销售规模，增强市场竞争力，同时，公司营业收入、净资产规模、净利润均有所提升。
需要注意的是，本次交易系溢价并购。以2025年12月31日为评估基准日，量羲技术净资产账面价值为8135.57万元，采用收益法评估的股东全部权益价值为6.87亿元，增值额约为6.06亿元，增值率为744.44%。本次交易完成后，公司将新增商誉约2.25亿元。
投融资专家许小恒表示，高商誉往往伴随高溢价并购，反映出交易定价中隐含的增长假设。若标的公司业绩不达预期，计提大额商誉减值将影响上市公司净利润。
02
保壳压力悬顶
拟并购重组背后，*ST禾信已被实施退市风险警示，存在退市风险。
从基本面来看，*ST禾信于2021年登陆科创板，然而，上市次年，公司业绩出现“变脸”。2022—2025年，*ST禾信净利连续四年处于亏损状态。因2025年度实现归属于上市公司股东的扣除非经常性损益前后的净利润孰低为负值，且2025年度实现扣除与主营业务无关的业务收入后营业收入低于1亿元，公司股票今年4月30日起被实施退市风险警示。
具体来看，2022—2025年，*ST禾信实现营业收入分别约为2.8亿元、3.66亿元、2.03亿元、9939.26万元；对应实现归属净利润分别约为-6332.83万元、-9610.61万元、-4599.09万元、-9480.18万元。
2026年1—6月，*ST禾信实现营业收入约为3469.92万元，同比下降34.3%；对应实现归属净利润约为-1943.8万元，同比增亏。对于今年上半年业绩变动情况，*ST禾信给出了两点解释，一是受政府采购周期阶段性收紧的影响，公司整体营业收入不及预期，整体毛利额仍不足以覆盖日常经营所需的刚性支出，进而形成经营亏损。二是公司控股子公司上海高端质谱仪器产业化项目于上年第四季度完成竣工并转入固定资产核算。受市场环境及投产节奏安排影响，该项目暂未实现全面投产运营，对应新增的折旧及费用化利息支出进一步加大了公司固定成本压力。
相比于*ST禾信过往业绩表现，标的公司量羲技术业绩表现亮眼。
财务数据显示，2024年、2025年，量羲技术实现营业收入分别约为7258.66万元、1.53亿元；对应实现归属净利润分别约为2197.47万元、5155.57万元。
据*ST禾信介绍，根据相关数据，交易完成后，2024年、2025年标的公司营业收入占合并后上市公司营业收入比例为26.39%、60.57%。
另外，股份发行情况方面，此次发行价格为17.6元/股，拟发行1395万股，占发行后上市公司总股本的比例为16.53%。截至9月24日收盘，*ST禾信报142.39元/股。与公司最新收盘价比，此次发行价格存在大幅折价。
针对相关问题，北京商报记者致电*ST禾信方面进行采访，不过电话未有人接听。

title: 'Scourge' of abuse must be rooted out, says Pope, during Lourdes visit
content:
Pope Leo has called on French bishops to root out the "scourge" of sexual abuse in the Roman Catholic church, telling them to "maintain the greatest vigilance", ahead of a meeting with abuse survivors.

The Pope delivered the message to bishops during a private meeting at the Sanctuary of Our Holy Lady of Lourdes, a holy site in southern France, on the third day of his four-day official visit to France.

A 2021 inquiry found that clergy or lay members of the Church had abused about 330,000 people as children in France over 70 years.

The Pope said Mass in front of thousands of worshippers in Lourdes, before he was scheduled to meet survivors of abuse privately later.

Before giving Mass the Pope told the bishops: "You have faced with determination the painful scourge of abuse of minors committed by members of the clergy or within an ecclesial context.

"It is important to persevere along the path you have begun, maintaining the greatest vigilance."

The gathering of senior church leaders was held behind closed doors and the remarks were later released to reporters.

The Lourdes gathering came a day after an estimated 700,000 people flocked to the Place de la Concorde in Paris to hear the pontiff speak.

Huge crowds cheered and waved as he rode down the Champs-Élysées Avenue greeting followers from his open-topped popemobile.

On Friday, the Pope also met French President Emmanuel Macron.

During Saturday's Mass in Paris, the Pope told worshippers that Catholics should not keep their faith to themselves but "let it overflow so that those you meet may be refreshed".

The leader of the Catholic Church also addressed young people in his speech, describing them as "today's Church".

"How beautiful it is to see your enthusiasm, energy and commitment, and the joy you bring to Christian communities," he said.

The number of regular worshippers in France has fallen from 35% of the population in 1960 to less than 5% today, while the number of priests has shrunk by two-thirds from 25,000 in 1990 to fewer than 9,000.

But in recent years there have been signs of a growing interest in religious tradition, with the number of adult baptisms more than doubling in five years to hit 10,000 in 2025.

Later on Sunday the Pope will meet staff and residents at the health facility at Lourdes, before taking part in a torchlight procession in the evening.

It is the Pope's first official visit to France since being chosen to lead the Roman Catholic church in May 2025.

Pope's have regularly visited France, a country with an avowedly secular modern political history but deep Catholic roots.

title: 盐湖股份的估值困局：业绩会上遭追问，股东催回购盼分红
content:
来源：华夏时报
华夏时报记者 胡雅文 北京报道
9月23日业绩会上，“市值管理”“回购”“加大信息透明度”成为 盐湖股份 （000792.SZ）被频繁追问的话题。2026年上半年，盐湖股份盈利61.69亿元，公司碳酸锂毛利率高达83.46%，明显高于 天齐锂业 与 赣锋锂业 的锂化合物及衍生品、锂系列产品毛利率，公司钾肥毛利率亦超过60%。
然而，市场并没有把盐湖股份视为锂业高成长龙头。截至9月24日，盐湖股份滚动市盈率仅在10倍出头，股价跌至23.7元/股，与业绩走势明显背离。在互动平台上，有投资者直言，“近期公司股价跌跌不休，与公司实际价值和经营业绩完全背离”，并追问“为什么不采取回购方式来管理市值？”对于众多疑问，盐湖股份方面告诉《华夏时报》记者，需要和相关负责同事确认回复进度。
业绩与股价背离
据 国联民生 证券测算，在盐湖股份2026年并表五矿盐湖后，公司碳酸锂年产能增至9.8万吨，产品生产成本进一步降低。今年上半年，盐湖股份的碳酸锂单吨售价为14.3万元，而其碳酸锂单吨生产成本仅2.4万元。2026年上半年，盐湖股份的锂盐和钾肥毛利均超过40亿元，公司上半年净利润同比翻倍至61.69亿元。
但市场并未买账。2026年4月，盐湖股份股价以39.29元/股收官。此后，其股价一路下跌，5月暴跌21.68%，7月大跌9.51%。截至9月24日，9月股价跌幅已接近16%。投资者等到了盐湖股份业绩变好，但公司股价却开始跌跌不休了，于是越来越多的股东开始询问公司市值管理、分红有关的问题。
公司管理层并未在业绩会上正面回应估值受压的原因，但公司并非没有表态。2026年，盐湖股份多次在互动平台阐述其管理举措，去年以来的具体措施包括：股份注销回购、实控人增持、优质锂资产收购、年产4万吨锂盐项目投产等方面，并表示，“资本市场受行业周期、市场环境多重因素影响，价格波动客观存在，后续公司将持续深耕钾锂主业，抓好生产经营、技术革新、资源拓展等重点工作，以扎实的发展成效回馈广大投资者。”
但投资者的不满在于，这些“多措并举”的表述相对笼统，缺乏可量化、可追踪的执行计划。股价持续下跌之下，有投资者仍在追问，公司为什么不直接采取回购方式管理市值？公司市值管理制度的具体执行情况如何？
股东催分红
截至今年6月末，盐湖股份资产负债表上趴着约323亿元货币资金，资产负债率为14.07%。公司对外也表示“经营性现金流充裕稳健”，但未直接回答为何没有新的回购计划。更突出的问题是分红缺位。公司称，由于母公司报表未分配利润尚未完全转正，公司尚未满足现金分红法定条件。尽管公司称已完成《公司章程》修订并建立《利润分配管理制度》《市值管理制度》，但投资者期待的实质性股东回报尚未到来。
过去，盐湖股份曾因多元化投资失利等问题面临经营困境，一度暂停上市。当时，公司投资近300亿元的金属镁一体化项目持续亏损，债务负担沉重，相关子公司面临重整。2017年，盐湖股份净利润断崖式下跌，2018年亏损34.47亿元，2019年巨亏458.6亿元。
万得数据显示，盐湖股份自2017年起停止分红。2019年至2025年，盐湖股份的未分配利润长期为负，但亏损金额逐渐收窄。2026年上半年，公司未分配利润已转正至45.64亿元。知名财税审专家、资深注册会计师刘志耕告诉《华夏时报》记者，“在分红问题上，尽管大股东可能主导决策，但小股东也有参与权和监督权。分红决策权通常由股东会或董事会掌握。股东会需审议并通过具体分红方案，确保方案符合法定条件，且需获得多数股东的同意。”
仍存同业竞争问题
更换控股股东及团队也是盐湖股份这几年经历的大变化。在中国五矿集团有限公司（下称“中国五矿”）入主盐湖股份后，2026年6月，雷志刚成为盐湖股份总经理。1972年生的雷志刚来自五矿体系，并非盐湖股份原有经营团队。2018年12月至2023年4月，他曾任长沙矿冶研究院有限责任公司党委副书记；2023年4月至2026年6月，他曾任湖南有色金属控股集团有限公司党委副书记、董事。
2026年，原由中国五矿控制的五矿盐湖已经并入盐湖股份，但青海汇信旗下的碳酸锂资产仍是悬而未决的同业竞争事项，这也是目前市场更关注的公司治理瑕疵。投资者多次质疑，“青海汇信用的就是盐湖股份的资源，为什么不直接收购？”
股权穿透后，中国五矿是青海汇信的实控人。2025年，青海汇信旗下年产2万吨碳酸锂生产装置建成投产，这代表青海汇信有了实际的碳酸锂产能，和盐湖股份一样向市场出售锂产品。更关键的是，其生产所需卤水由盐湖股份按市场价格供应。也就是说，盐湖股份在向竞争对手出售核心原材料，而竞争对手用这些原料生产碳酸锂，双方存在同业竞争关系。
盐湖股份今年6月曾表示，实控人及控股股东前期已就同业竞争作出明确承诺，公司将积极推动相关工作，目前不存在影响生产经营的重大不利的同业竞争情形。根据公开资料，中国五矿承诺在2030年1月14日之前解决同业竞争问题，目前距离承诺到期还有约3年多时间。
不过，从这次业绩会来看，相对格式化的回答仍未消除投资者疑虑，股东更关心的是公司有没有阶段性的具体安排，以及公司能否给出足以让市场重新评估公司的实质性信号。

title: The India shock: exporting workers to the world
content:
Tej Parikh

Published September 27 2026

This article is an on-site version of the Free Lunch newsletter. Premium subscribers can sign up here to get the newsletter delivered every Thursday and Sunday. Standard subscribers can upgrade to Premium here , or explore all FT newsletters

India has its own version of the “China shock”. Instead of exporting high volumes of competitive manufacturing goods across the globe, the world’s most populous nation sends millions of workers abroad.

India churns out roughly 5mn graduates each year and around 1mn people enter its workforce every month. But just as the Chinese economy lacks the demand to absorb more of its industrial production at home, India’s cannot produce enough suitable jobs to employ its expanding labour supply. Youth underemployment is rife, despite the country’s rapid growth rate.

Some content could not load. Check your internet connection or browser settings.

As a result, many Indians, often well-educated and English-speaking, move abroad to pursue careers. The country is the world’s largest source of international migrants, with an estimated 18.5mn living abroad in 2024. The Anglosphere and United Arab Emirates are common destinations.

Indeed, over the past decade, Indian nationals have accounted for the vast majority of approved H-1B petitions, a US visa for global professionals in selected fields. In the UK, about 1mn Indian nationals arrived between 2021 and 2025. Meanwhile, last year Indians overtook the English for the first time to become Australia’s largest overseas-born group.

Some content could not load. Check your internet connection or browser settings.

Under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the country has positioned its large labour force — which includes the world’s second-biggest pool of science, technology, engineering and mathematics (Stem) graduates — as an answer to skills shortages and ageing demographics abroad.

S Jaishankar, India’s foreign minister, recently said the country had signed labour-mobility pacts with 26 countries, with more in the pipeline. Such arrangements have been a central pillar of India’s bilateral trade negotiations. An overseas mobility bill also aims to help Indians access the “global workplace”.

This strategy has several upsides for New Delhi. At around $150bn last year, 3 per cent of its GDP, the country is by far the largest recipient of remittance payments. Returnees and the overseas community are sources of foreign exchange, investment and knowhow for the country. This summer, domestic banks raised more than $50bn by encouraging the diaspora, the world’s largest, to shift savings to India as part of measures to shore up the rupee.

Crucially, as with China’s overproduction, overseas markets provide a release valve. The export of workers enables the Indian government to ease socio-economic strains at home, where frustration abounds over the lack of good job opportunities.

Some content could not load. Check your internet connection or browser settings.

But there are drawbacks to the worker-export model. For example, one estimate suggests brain drain costs India between $35bn and $50bn per annum, owing in part to lost productivity growth. Many Indians end up settling abroad.

And just as China is experiencing a worldwide backlash against its exports, India faces one as well.

Scepticism about immigration continues to animate politics in the rich world. And the recent surge in arrivals from the subcontinent, who join historical waves of emigration, puts a growing spotlight on people of Indian origin abroad.

Relative to native-born citizens and other migrant populations, Indian-born migrants and people of Indian heritage tend to obtain higher levels of education and earnings. Their rising prominence in public life — as chief executives, politicians and heads of prestigious organisations — can drive animosity. And though Indian nationals often dominate high-skilled immigration routes, family members and less-skilled individuals have emigrated too, in some cases by abusing the rules. This all provides fuel for anti-immigrant narratives.

Some content could not load. Check your internet connection or browser settings.

Indeed, anti-Indian sentiment is on the rise. Just this month, the Republican nominee for a seat on Texas’s oil and gas regulator sparked allegations of racism for a social media post aimed at South Asian students. Last year, Indian-origin migrants were explicitly targeted in “March for Australia” rallies. Anti-South Asian slurs in online spaces in the US have also surged . The backlash could hinder the Modi government’s strategy. As it happens, US President Donald Trump has raised scrutiny of and fees for H-1B visas.

The “India shock” has implications for both sides. Rich economies need talented young workers. But a policy of immigration warrants robust administration, investment in housing and public services and initiatives to encourage integration and cohesion. Otherwise it won’t be sustainable.

India, meanwhile, cannot rely on remittances and its diaspora alone. The worker-export model reflects a deeper challenge facing New Delhi, which must strive to create enough productive work to better harness the country’s demographic dividend. China lacks consumer confidence. India lacks jobs. Neither can export its way out of domestic problems.

title: Will US jobs data add to pressure on Fed policymakers?
content:
George Steer in New York, Olaf Storbeck in Frankfurt and Leo Lewis in Tokyo

Published September 27 2026

Could you be the FT’s top trader?

Next week will be capped off by a flurry of US labour market data set to land just as simmering inflation and signs of economic overheating are combining to push Treasury yields to multi-decade highs.

Thirty-year US Treasury yields, which are driven by rising inflation expectations, surged this week to their highest level since June 2004 after a report published on Wednesday showed business activity accelerated in September at the fastest pace in five years.

The 10-year Treasury yield, which sets borrowing costs across the globe, rose to its highest since 2007 as remarks by Federal Reserve policymakers added to concerns that higher interest rates will be required to cool the US economy.

The Fed last month raised rates for the first time since 2023 — by a quarter point to a range of 3.75 per cent to 4 per cent — with new chair Kevin Warsh using his press conference to flag the strength of the economy and the labour market.

Data to be released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics on Friday is expected to show the US added 100,000 jobs in September, which would mark a slowdown from the 162,000 new jobs added in August.

Economists polled by Reuters expect the data also to show that the US unemployment rate rose to 4.2 per cent in September from 4.1 per cent in August.

Bank of America strategists are forecasting just 60,000 new jobs and the unemployment rate to hold steady at 4.1 per cent, which they said would ease pressure on the Fed to raise rates again in October. George Steer

With natural gas prices having shot up to their highest level since late 2022 and oil prices hovering above $100 a barrel, euro area inflation is widely expected to have got another shot in the arm in September, strengthening the case for a third interest rate rise by the European Central Bank.

Economists polled by Reuters expect consumer prices in September to have risen by 3.5 per cent year on year, up from 3.2 per cent in August, the fastest pace in close to three years, when Eurostat publishes its flash estimate on Friday.

That would leave inflation above the ECB’s medium-term target of 2 per cent for the seventh month in a row. Analysts are also bracing for higher core inflation, which excludes volatile energy and food prices and is forecast to have risen to 2.6 per cent, a level briefly seen in May.

The central bank raised interest rates this month to 2.5 per cent, and markets are pricing in a nearly 50 per cent chance of another rise next month, with one rise fully priced in and a 30 per cent chance of a second by the end of the year.

“This uptick [in inflation] is not primarily due to the transmission of higher energy costs,” Morgan Stanley economists wrote in a note to clients on Friday, adding that it partly reflects volatility in tourism. Airfares and accommodation costs softened in August and are likely to rebound in September, they said.

Energy prices are likely to have risen “steeply” by an annual pace of close to 18 per cent, after a 14 per cent rise in August, Morgan Stanley added. But despite such eye-watering numbers, inflation trends so far seem to be in line with the ECB’s baseline scenario.

“This would support our conviction that the next ECB move will come in December, and not October,” the analysts said. Olaf Storbeck

The Bank of Japan’s quarterly Tankan survey of business sentiment on Thursday will provide a snapshot of the economy at a particularly turbulent time, as companies relish the greater pricing power they have gained with the end of deflation but face fragile consumer confidence as inflation starts to bite.

The BoJ has raised interest rates to their highest level in 31 years but the yen remains persistently weak and seemingly resistant to attempts by the government to talk or manipulate it higher.

Companies’ responses to the survey were taken around September 9 — before the BoJ’s interest rate decision but at a time when a 0.25 percentage point rise was deemed a virtual certainty.

Analysts expect the sentiment of large manufacturers to have improved in the most recent quarter, while that of non-manufacturers is likely to have dropped modestly while remaining high.

Analysts at Morgan Stanley MUFG said they would focus on any signals of the early impact of the BoJ’s tightening — such as improvement in capital expenditure plans among small and medium-sized non-manufacturers, which were revised down unusually sharply in the June Tankan survey. Leo Lewis
